topic: 5 things to leave at home on your first bikepacking trip

content.hook: 5 things to leave home on your first bikepacking trip

slides.title: 5 things to *leave at home*
slides.body: Your first bikepacking trip, a little lighter.

slides.title: The *'just in case'* pile
slides.body: Pack for the conditions you expect. Extra outfits mostly add weight.

slides.title: *Cotton* everything
slides.body: It stays damp and dries slowly. Pick quick-dry layers instead.

slides.title: The *backpack*
slides.body: Let the bike carry the load. Your back and shoulders will thank you.

slides.title: Spare *gadgets*
slides.body: Bring what you will actually use. Every extra cable adds weight.

slides.title: Over-ambitious *daily distance*
slides.body: Heat, wind and surface slow you down. Plan realistic days, not just kilometres.

slides.title: Plan *realistic days*, pack the right gear

content.caption:
Your first bikepacking trip doesn't need more stuff. It needs the right stuff.

Here's what to leave at home:

1. The "just in case" pile. Pack for the conditions you expect, not every possibility.
2. Cotton everything. It stays damp and dries slowly. Quick-dry layers are the better pick.
3. The backpack. Let the bike carry the load, not your shoulders.
4. Spare gadgets. If you won't use it, it's just weight.
5. Over-ambitious daily distance. Heat, wind and rough surface slow you down. Plan realistic days.

Lighter bags, easier days, more fun. Most of us learn this the slow way, on a hill.

Save this for your packing day.

If you like planning ahead: BikepackPilot splits your route into 50 km segments. You set surface, heat, wind and rain for each one. It then calculates realistic riding days and adapts its gear recommendations to the conditions you entered.
